races.title: State House, District 83
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Grant Campbell
cands.bio: Physician and U.S. Army veteran who retired as a lieutenant colonel after tours in Iraq, Kuwait and Afghanistan. He was vice chairman of the N.C. State Board of Community Colleges. Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 83 (Cabarrus and Rowan counties) since January 2025.

endorsements.text: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Campbell listed endorsements from Reps. Kristin Baker, Harry Warren, David Willis, Dean Arp and Howard Penny, Sen. Paul Newton, and COL (Ret) Russ Olson. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: We found no bills he sponsored, no votes cast, and no actions in office on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, abortion, or Red Flag laws. His campaign site speaks to economic development in general terms but says nothing on data centers or growth limits. It describes opposing "government control over personal healthcare decisions" without addressing abortion. His campaign site gives his stance on border security only in connection with fentanyl. We found no documented land-use stances, no controversies, no foreign ties, and no 2026 endorsements. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. His place of upbringing within North Carolina and the year he came to live in his district are not stated in the pages we read.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia gives his birthplace as Sanford, NC, his campaign biography says he was born and raised in North Carolina, and he earned both his undergraduate and medical degrees at UNC Chapel Hill.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Physician in private practice for more than 25 years, with Army service as a trauma surgeon. Member of the NC House since 2025. Former vice chairman of the State Board of Community Colleges, which does not count toward this score.
qual.why: He has one term of legislative service and a long professional career as a physician. That career is outside law, policy or budget work, so the score sits in the upper-middle range rather than the high one.
qual.label: He has one term of legislative service and a long professional career as a physician. That career is outside law, policy or budget work, so the score sits in the upper-middle range rather than the high one.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he supports school choice, including Opportunity Scholarships, and higher teacher salaries tied to objective measures of job performance.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he supports stronger penalties for assaulting law-enforcement officers, resisting arrest and fleeing a crime scene, and says prosecutors must be held accountable, including for enforcing bail requirements and prosecuting repeat offenders.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says the right to keep and bear arms is constitutionally guaranteed "full stop" and that restrictions on law-abiding citizens do nothing to reduce gun violence.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

cands.name: Johnnie Jones
cands.bio: Retired blue-collar worker from Davidson, NC. Worked in construction, upholstery and furniture, film and commercials (IATSE Local 491 member from 2000), and automotive and racing until retiring in 2021. Democratic candidate for NC House District 83 in 2026. Has held no public office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Black Political Caucus of Cabarrus County, N.C.; Down Home North Carolina; and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (a voting group run by Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Johnnie Jones was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. His campaign site says his mother worked for the Statesville school system and he now lives in Davidson, but neither source states his upbringing. He has held no public office, so there is no record of bills, votes or official actions. We found nothing on his positions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. On healthcare, Ballotpedia says he supports expanding Medicaid, but that is outside the listed topics. We found no news coverage or controversies about him.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Worked in construction, upholstery and furniture, then film and commercial work as a union member from 2000, then automotive and racing until retiring in August 2021. He has no record of elected office, legislative work or policy staff work.
qual.why: He has a long work record, but it is in trades and entertainment rather than law, policy, budgets or elected office. That puts him in the low band for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: He has a long work record, but it is in trades and entertainment rather than law, policy, budgets or elected office. That puts him in the low band for writing law and the state budget.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Says AI data centers deplete water and deforest land, get power subsidies while public rates rise, and "need to be halted and reviewed now"; he supports an environmental survey before any construction is considered.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign platform: AI data centers "need to be halted and reviewed now"; he supports more research, an environmental survey before construction can be considered, and community-led answers.

Ballotpedia survey: he is committed to protecting communities and requiring restrictions and additional oversight, including expanded environmental review, for hyperscale AI data centers proposed in nearby areas despite public disapproval.
